parsedVerdict.reasoning:
AdvanceOrderUseCase.execute only orchestrates. It loads the order through the repository port, hands the state transition to the domain (order.advanceTo), coordinates a domain service (stock.dispatch when the target is 'shipped'), saves through the port and maps the result to a DTO. That is the job of the application layer. The state machine itself stays in the domain. The file has no persistence, HTTP handling, framework logic or business rules of its own.

The one smell is the optional `request?: Request` parameter, typed with express's Request. It is never read, so the file does no transport work with it. Importing a framework is a dependency-direction question, which the rubric puts out of scope, and the symbolic checker already sees the express IMPORTS edge. Leaving the parameter in the signature is still poor hygiene.

The dispatch-on-shipped check is a use case deciding which domain service to call, which is ordinary application work.
